sections.content: How many people stayed in Newport (Telford and Wrekin) after gaining qualifications?

Newport (Telford and Wrekin) is a small town in the West Midlands. Newport (Telford and Wrekin) does not have its own university.

Newport (Telford and Wrekin) has lower levels of deprivation.

Overall, Newport (Telford and Wrekin) ended up with:

  • fewer graduates than it produced
  • fewer non-graduates with advanced qualifications than it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 605 state-school pupils from Newport (Telford and Wrekin) who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 245 (40%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 190 (31%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Newport (Telford and Wrekin) to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Newport (Telford and Wrekin)'s pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Newport (Telford and Wrekin) in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Newport (Telford and Wrekin) move to?

Of Newport (Telford and Wrekin)'s graduates, 140 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

Of Newport (Telford and Wrekin)'s qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 80 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 35 of those qualified non-graduates (44%) were living fairly locally, in the Telford travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Newport (Telford and Wrekin)'s GCSE cohort:

  • 90 graduates left the West Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 25 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the West Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 37% of graduates and 38% of qualified non-graduates living in Newport (Telford and Wrekin) had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 150 graduates and 170 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Newport (Telford and Wrekin). This is compared with the 245 graduates and 190 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 67% of the graduates had also lived in Newport (Telford and Wrekin) as GCSE pupils, while 37% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Newport (Telford and Wrekin) in 2018 to 2019, 62% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 38% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
